source.title: The amygdala's role in long-term declarative memory for gist and detail.

confidence_rationale: Direct human lesion evidence for a double dissociation between gist and detail memory under amygdala damage, which is the exact content-selective (not scalar) signature MECH-074b requires. Confidence held below 0.8 because (a) the effect appeared only under bilateral (n=1 rare case) not unilateral damage, and (b) the study measures an encoding/filtering role, not the specific retrieval-time per-trace weight vector MECH-074b posits.
failure_signatures: Unilateral amygdala damage did NOT produce the gist/detail dissociation; only bilateral damage did, and the bilateral finding rests on a single rare patient -- so the effect magnitude and reliability in humans is anchored by n=1.

The authors frame the amygdala's role as filtering the ENCODING of relevant information; the paper provides no evidence that the dissociation is generated by a retrieval-time weight applied to already-stored hippocampal traces (MECH-074b's specific locus).

mapping.source_claim_statement: Bilateral, but not unilateral, damage to the amygdala results in poorer memory for gist but superior memory for visual detail of aversive scenes; the amygdala may help filter the encoding of relevant information from stimuli that signal threat or danger.
mapping.ree_translation: The double dissociation (gist down, detail up under amygdala loss) is the behavioural hallmark that MECH-074b's vector-not-scalar retrieval weight is built to reproduce: a scalar retrieval gain applied to all traces would raise gist AND detail together and could never produce the opposite-direction change in peripheral/detail memory. The paper therefore supports the CONTENT-SELECTIVE form of the BLA->hippocampus modulation (w_i differs by trace salience) over the named scalar-gain failure signature.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper localises the effect to encoding-time filtering, whereas MECH-074b asserts a RETRIEVAL-time per-trace weight that grows with trace age (20 min -> 1 week). This source cannot distinguish an encoding-selection account from a retrieval-weighting account; it constrains only that the modulation is content-selective, not where in the encode/retrieve cycle the selection is applied.
mapping.source_context: Human neuropsychology; 20 unilateral + 1 bilateral amygdala-damage patients vs 15 brain-damaged and 47 healthy controls; long-term declarative memory for gist vs visual detail of aversive and neutral scenes.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (well-controlled lesion study, canonical result, human data). Mapping fidelity moderate-high: the gist/detail dissociation directly falsifies scalar gain, but the encode-vs-retrieve locus is unresolved. Transfer risk moderate: human declarative-memory task -> REE hippocampal proposal/recall scores is a reasonable but non-trivial mapping.
